title: Laws compared
question: What does each binding government instrument that addresses developers of frontier or general-purpose AI models say on the same questions?
introduction: Each row is one instrument. Each column is one question, worded so that it fits every instrument. The questions are Selekoa’s; an instrument’s own terms appear only in quotation marks.

legend.stated: A passage of the instrument meets the question’s criterion as worded, however conditional or narrow its scope. The condition or scope is in the note.
legend.partly: A passage has what the criterion asks for, but in a weaker form than the criterion’s own words: for example, a power (“may”) where the criterion asks for a duty (“shall”), or a duty without the deadline the question asks about.
legend.not-found: No passage meeting the criterion was found. The cell lists the sections read, the search terms and every passage set aside, with the reason. It does not show that the instrument lacks such a provision elsewhere, or that no other law imposes one.
legend.not-applicable: The question does not arise for this instrument, for the reason given (for example, there is no framework duty whose publication could be asked about).
legend.not-retrieved: The instrument’s text could not be retrieved, so the question could not be checked.
legend.held: The cross-family checker and the preparer disagree on the status. The cell shows the preparer’s status and is held, with both reasons, for the maintainer’s decision.

rules: Every stated or partly cell quotes the instrument’s own official text, with its article, section or page. Explainers by law firms or the press are not evidence.
Dates keep their kind and precision: adoption, signature, approval, publication, entry into force and application are different events.
A requirement is not evidence that any developer complied with it, or that any named developer falls within a category.
No ranking, scoring or characterisation of instruments. Rows are in a fixed order by jurisdiction, then date.
Biological and chemical risk provisions are recorded at policy level only.

questions.question: On whom does the instrument place the duties compared here, in its own defined terms?
questions.criterion: The defined term for the party that bears the duties (developer, provider, company, exporter), quoted from its definition or from the provision that imposes the duties. Where the instrument has tiers, each tier is named in its own defined terms.

questions.question: What threshold or condition brings a model, or its developer, within those duties?
questions.criterion: A stated condition, quoted with its figure where there is one: training compute, compute cost, revenue, capability, number of users, or designation by an authority. Stated if a threshold or designation condition is quoted; partly if the instrument covers a broad class (for example, all public services of a kind) without any model-level threshold.

questions.question: Must the covered party write or adopt a document setting out how it assesses and manages risks from its models?
questions.criterion: A provision requiring the covered party to have a written framework, policy or protocol on the risks of its models. A policy on a single other subject (copyright, content labelling) does not meet it. Partly if a risk-management system or measures are required without a written document.

questions.question: Must that document be published, or given to a public authority?
questions.criterion: A provision requiring the document in Q03 to be published, or submitted or made available to a public authority. Not applicable where Q03 finds no such document.

questions.question: Must the covered party evaluate or test its models for risks?
questions.criterion: A duty to assess, evaluate or test the model for risks, before or after it is made available. Partly if the duty is to assess something other than the model (for example, a service or a content category) or is stated only as an aim.

questions.question: Does the instrument require, or provide for, assessment of the model or of the developer’s practices by anyone other than the developer?
questions.criterion: Stated if the instrument requires an assessment by an independent or external party or by a public authority. Partly if it only permits or empowers one (an authority “may” evaluate or request access), or provides for an assessment of filings or documents rather than of the model.

questions.question: Must the covered party report incidents to a public authority, and within what time?
questions.criterion: A duty to report incidents, defined however the instrument defines them, to a named public authority. The deadline is quoted where stated. Partly if a reporting duty has no stated deadline, or runs to someone other than a public authority.

questions.question: Must the covered party publish, or give an authority, information about each model?
questions.criterion: A duty to publish a report on a model, or to draw up and supply documentation on it to an authority or to others, quoted with its trigger (for example, before deployment). A labelling or watermark duty on outputs does not meet it; it is noted where present.

questions.question: Does the instrument protect people who report risks or violations?
questions.criterion: A provision prohibiting retaliation against employees or others who disclose risks or violations, or requiring a channel for such disclosures. A general complaint mechanism for users is noted but does not meet the criterion. Partly if the protection applies only by reference to another law.

questions.question: When was the instrument adopted, signed, approved or issued, according to its own text or official record?
questions.criterion: A date with its kind, quoted from the instrument or the official legislative or gazette record. Dates of other kinds (publication, entry into force) go in Q11 and Q12.

questions.question: When does the instrument enter into force or take effect, by its own provision?
questions.criterion: The instrument’s own provision on entry into force, taking effect or operative date, quoted. A date computed from a rule (“the twentieth day following publication”) is quoted as the rule; any computed date is marked as computed.

questions.question: From when do the duties compared here apply, where the instrument sets a date or period different from entry into force?
questions.criterion: A provision setting a separate application date or transition period for the duties compared here, including for models already on the market. Not found if no separate date is located; the cell does not infer one.

questions.question: What is the maximum penalty for breaching the duties, and on what basis is it set?
questions.criterion: A quoted maximum (amount, share of turnover, or other measure) with its basis, such as per violation or a percentage of turnover. Partly if the instrument provides for penalties without a stated maximum, or by reference to another law.

questions.question: Which public body enforces or supervises the duties?
questions.criterion: A named public body given power to enforce, supervise or penalise breaches of the duties compared here, quoted.

questions.question: Does the instrument require, recognise or refer to a developer’s own safety framework, or to a code of practice or standard, and how?
questions.criterion: A provision that requires a developer’s framework, names a code of practice or standard as a means of showing compliance, deems compliance with another regime to be compliance, or otherwise refers to such documents. The relation is recorded in the instrument’s own words: requires, may rely on, deemed, refers to.

partlyRules: An order to an agency to impose a duty counts as partly.
Protection only by reference to another law counts as partly.
“Without undue delay” counts as a stated deadline.
Required security measures for model weights count as risk-management measures under Q03.
partlyRulesBasis: Decision 5a, approved by the maintainer on 2026-11-03 (review note, “Maintainer decisions”).
